review_notes: I read the whole target file and the simp-tagged lemmas in the imported FiniteTargetHomColimit.lean (stageHomEquiv_apply, stageHomEquiv_symm_apply, stageHomToContinuous_class, and others). I did not run Lean. The findings rest on simp's inside-out rewriting order and on a lemma set that I only read. I did not search for downstream uses of these lemmas.

findings.excerpt: stageHomLimitEquiv F c hc G d hd f = stageHomLimitMap F c hc G d f := rfl
findings.problem: This simp lemma rewrites the equivalence applied to f into the raw map stageHomLimitMap. Simp rewrites inner terms first, so in `(stageHomLimitEquiv ..).symm (stageHomLimitEquiv .. f)` the inner application becomes `stageHomLimitMap .. f` before the generic `Equiv.symm_apply_apply` can match. The file has no simp lemma for `(stageHomLimitEquiv ..).symm (stageHomLimitMap .. f) = f`, so the round trip stays unreduced. The lemma also unfolds the equivalence into an implementation function, which makes the normal form depend on how the equivalence was built.
findings.proposed_change: Either remove `@[simp]` from stageHomLimitEquiv_apply, or keep it and add `@[simp] theorem stageHomLimitEquiv_symm_stageHomLimitMap (f : c.pt ⟶ d.pt) : (stageHomLimitEquiv F c hc G d hd).symm (stageHomLimitMap F c hc G d f) = f`. The second option can be proved with `(stageHomLimitEquiv F c hc G d hd).symm_apply_apply f`. If the lemma is kept, also add the matching `stageHomLimitMap (symm x) = x` statement, so that both round trips normalise.
findings.benefit: Round trips through the equivalence simplify to `f` or `x` instead of getting stuck on `stageHomLimitMap`. Users get one canonical form for the equivalence.

findings.excerpt:
(stageHomLimitMap F c hc G d f).val j =
      (stageHomEquiv c hc (G.obj j)).symm (f ≫ d.π.app j) := rfl
findings.problem: Both lemmas are simp and they overlap. The inner term `(stageHomLimitMap ..).val j` in the left side of `stageHomLimitMap_toContinuous` is itself an instance of the left side of `stageHomLimitMap_apply`. Simp rewrites that inner term first, so the outer `stageHomLimitMap_toContinuous` rarely fires. The proof of that lemma is `by simp`, which only goes through apply followed by `stageHomEquiv_symm_apply`. Even when the outer lemma does fire, the rewrite `stageHomEquiv_symm_apply` gives the same result. The apply lemma also expands a section component into `.symm` of an equivalence applied to `f ≫ d.π.app j`. That is an implementation-level form. It can obscure the intended `stageHomClass` description, because it only reduces when the argument has the shape `c.π.app i ≫ map g`.
findings.proposed_change: Keep one canonical rewrite. Either drop `@[simp]` from `stageHomLimitMap_apply` and keep `stageHomLimitMap_toContinuous` as the simp lemma that characterises the component, or keep apply as the simp lemma and drop `@[simp]` from the redundant `stageHomLimitMap_toContinuous`. The first option needs the proof of `stageHomLimitMap_toContinuous` rewritten with explicit `rw [stageHomLimitMap_apply, stageHomEquiv_symm_apply]`.
findings.benefit: This gives a single predictable normal form and removes a lemma that simp cannot use in practice. It also avoids exposing the `stageHomEquiv.symm` implementation when the section component is only used through its continuous representative.
